validity.recommendation: Flag for review as a possible phantom/GEM-only entity before further data investment. The row's entire traceable basis is a single 2018 news-media infographic that GEM's own page says shows the line only as 'prospective' and explicitly absent from Gazprom's own 2019 Annual Report; no independent Russian-language or English-language source (Gazprom, Sakhatransneftegaz, Sakha Republic government, Glavgosexpertiza, neftegaz.ru, TASS, Interfax, regional Yakutia press) names a distinct 'Yakutsk-Aldan' gas pipeline project. Recommend either retiring the row, reclassifying as unconfirmed, or holding it open pending a source that actually names the project -- do not treat any of its currently-blank fields as normal research backlog until existence is settled.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's own P2706 wiki page (read for leads only, never cited) carries exactly TWO harvested citations and states its entire case in one paragraph: 'A pipeline running from Yakutsk to Aldan is shown as a "prospective gas pipeline" on a Financial Times graphic from April 3, 2018. However, it is not shown on the Gazprom 2019 Annual Report... As of July 2022, there have been no further news about this project, and it appears to be cancelled.' So GEM's cite #1 (Gazprom 2019 Annual Report PDF, gazprom.com) is cited to document an ABSENCE, not a confirmation, and GEM's cite #2 is the FT interactive graphic accompanying 'Russia's $55bn pipeline gamble on China's demand for gas' (ig.ft.com/gazprom-pipeline-power-of-siberia/) -- the SAME article whose headline figure is almost certainly the source of the implausible $55bn SegmentCost already flagged as a likely aggregate-cost defect on sibling row P2352 (Power of Siberia Phase I), i.e. this exact graphic is already known in this batch to be a source of miscalibrated/aggregated figures, not a primary engineering document. I could not independently view the graphic itself: ig.ft.com returned an HTTP 302 (subscription wall) to a plain curl and WebFetch refused the ft.com domain outright, so I cannot confirm what the graphic's 'Yakutsk-Aldan' label actually depicts or whether it is a genuine standalone route versus a simplified regional label. Ran extensive Russian-language searches for a dedicated project ('газопровод Якутск Алдан', '"Якутск-Алдан" трубопровод проект') across Russian news, government and trade-press indexes: found nothing naming a distinct Yakutsk-Aldan gas pipeline. What DOES exist near Aldan is different infrastructure: Gazprom's South/West Yakutia gasification programme taps the Power of Siberia trunk (P2352/P2353) with four short branch pipelines (газопроводы-отводы) feeding gas-distribution stations (ГРС) 'Aldan', 'Aldan-2', 'Мурья' and 'Чульман' (neftegaz.ru, yakutia.info, yakutia-daily.ru, yk24.ru, Sept 2026 reporting) -- local distribution spurs OFF the Power of Siberia trunk near where it already passes through Aldan district, not a 466 km trunk originating at Yakutsk city. Critically, Yakutsk city itself is not on the Power of Siberia route at all (that trunk runs Chayanda field/Lensky district -> Aldan/Olekminsk/Neryungri districts -> Amur Oblast, well south of Yakutsk); Yakutsk's own gas supply comes from the wholly separate Srednevilyuyskoye-Yakutsk system, already recorded as 8 other rows on this same roster (P2334, P3361, P3364, P3365, P6691, P6694, P6695, P6696). A direct ~466 km gas trunk connecting Yakutsk city to Aldan town therefore does not correspond to any real gas corridor I could find any evidence of -- it reads as a plausible misreading of a simplified news graphic rather than a documented engineering project. I checked the 32-row Far East roster for a possible relabeled duplicate (e.g. a segment of P2352/P2353 or one of the Aldan-area feeder rows P6682/P3896/P6710/P7600) but none matches this row's stated termini (Yakutsk city -> Aldan district) closely enough to call it the same physical entity under another name, so I am not filing a duplicate flag -- existence is the primary open question, not misattribution to a sibling PID.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Cannot properly evaluate whether 'cancelled' is the right status because the underlying question is existence, not dormancy: see the existence concern in validity[]. GEM's own narrative already frames this as an inference from an 8-year news silence following a single 2018 FT graphic that showed the line as merely 'prospective' -- normally that pattern (proposed, no progress, long silence) is exactly the dormancy rule's 'shelved >=4y -> cancelled' case, and if the project is treated at face value as having been proposed, 'cancelled' with ShelvedCancelledType='inferred' would be the mechanically correct application of that rule. But I was unable to find ANY independent source (Russian or English) that ever names a distinct 'Yakutsk-Aldan' gas pipeline project in the first place, so I cannot confirm there was ever a real proposal to become dormant and then cancelled, as opposed to a media graphic's simplified regional label being reified into a GEM entry that never corresponded to an actual project. Recommend resolving the existence question before finalizing Status or ShelvedCancelledType; if the row is retained on the strength of the FT graphic alone, ShelvedCancelledType='inferred' (never 'confirmed') would be the honest value, with CancelledYear left blank since no source states one.

summary: P2706 Yakutsk-Aldan Gas Pipeline: EXISTENCE CONCERN -- sole traceable basis is a single 2018 FT graphic GEM itself says is absent from Gazprom's own annual report, and no independent Russian or English source names a distinct Yakutsk-Aldan gas pipeline (the real Aldan-area gas infrastructure is unrelated short Power-of-Siberia distribution branches, not a 466 km Yakutsk-city trunk); all 14 worklist units addressed (1 validity existence concern + 13 UNRESOLVED fills/status-review, all tied to that concern).
